stemBlocks.value: Solve the simultaneous equations 2x + y = 8 and x − y = 1 graphically. (a) Express each equation in the form y = mx + c. (b) Draw both graphs on the grid provided. (c) State the solution.
Think first: Rearranging into y = mx + c first tells you the gradient and intercept, which makes plotting quick and safe.

contentBlocks.value: Result: Three points for each line

solutionSteps.instruction: Plot and join both lines on the grid.

contentBlocks.value: Use a ruler and label each line with its equation
The lines meet where -2x + 8 = x − 1, i.e. at x = 3, y = 2

solutionSteps.instruction: Check the solution in both original equations.

strategyBlocks.value: Make y the subject of each equation, build a small table of values for each, draw both lines on the grid and read the point where they cross.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (a) y = -2x + 8 and y = x − 1  (b) Both straight lines drawn on the grid  (c) x = 3, y = 2.

whyThisWorks.value: Each equation describes a whole line of (x, y) pairs; the pair that works for both equations must lie on both lines, so it is the crossing point. Putting the equations in the form y = mx + c does not change which points satisfy them, it just makes the gradient and y-intercept visible so the lines can be plotted accurately.

commonErrors.misconception: Sign slips when rearranging: writing y = 2x + 8 instead of y = -2x + 8.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Sign slips when rearranging: writing y = 2x + 8 instead of y = -2x + 8.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading x − y = 1 as y = 1 − x rather than y = x − 1.

examTip.value: Always substitute your graphical solution back into both original equations — it takes ten seconds and turns a read-off into a checked answer.
